question:
(i) Explain how symmetry helps in applying Gauss’s law to find electric field.
(ii) For the following charge distributions, name the suitable Gaussian surface: an infinitely long uniformly charged wire, an infinite plane sheet of charge and a uniformly charged spherical shell.

options.A:
(i) Symmetry is not useful in Gauss’s law
(ii) Wire: spherical surface; sheet: spherical surface; shell: cylindrical surface
options.B:
(i) Symmetry makes the enclosed charge zero
(ii) Wire: pillbox; sheet: coaxial cylinder; shell: cube
options.C:
(i) Symmetry allows a Gaussian surface on which $E$ has constant magnitude or a simple direction, simplifying flux
(ii) Wire: coaxial cylinder; sheet: pillbox cylinder; shell: concentric sphere
options.D:
(i) Symmetry is used only to calculate charge density
(ii) Wire: plane surface; sheet: toroid; shell: open hemisphere
